newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases to 8.3 pct from 8.6.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases to 8.3 pct from 8.6.

text.p: Average lending rate edged down to 8.3 from 8.6 percent as lenders mostly kept rates flat in thin money market trade.
Dealers said total settlements were 25 million kuna, with demand at 32 million which could not be completely satisfied. Supply slackened to 55 million kuna.
New loans accounted for 14.2 million kuna, of which most was interbank call money money made at a steady 8.0 percent. The rate for seven day interbank funds was 11 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous shorter loans at 7.0 percent, and one smaller 15-30 day laon at 12 percent.
Overnight trade totalled 99.3 million kuna, of which 95 million went to two banks for maintenance of their reserve payment. The rest was granted to three banks with shortfalls.

The central bank said it stayed out of the hard currency market. It calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday slightly weaker at 5.3766 against the dollar and at 3.5583 versus the mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
